newsitem.title: USA: Maine considers $50 mln note sale in August.
newsitem.headline: Maine considers $50 mln note sale in August.

text.p: Maine might sell about $50 million of tax anticipation notes in August, said the state treasurer on Tuesday, noting the state's improved finances enabled Maine to make this an option instead of a necessity.

Dale McCormick told Reuters Financial Television in an interview: "What I am very proud of is that this next fiscal year, at the end of this fiscal year, we for the first time in years, will not have to go out for a TAN the next day of the fiscal year, July 1. We will have enough revenue and enough cushion that we won't have to do that."
She added: "And in fact we will have the ability to choose whether or not we're going to do a TAN. And if we do one, it will probably be in August."
Parts of the interview with McCormick are scheduled to be aired on Thursday at 1515 EDT.

Maine has a $3.8 billion biennial budget for fiscal 1998 and fiscal 1999, which raises spending by a modest amount from the previous pact, according to Standard and Poor's Corp, which gave the state an AA-plus rating.
The state on Wednesday is selling its only general obligation bond offering for this year, a $42.7 million debt sale through a syndicate led by PaineWebber.

While the state has an approximately $2.6 billion unfunded pension obligation, McCormick said the gap was closing as the value of assets climbed, adding the King Administration had no plans to sell bonds to pay off the liability.
"The retirement system would have the call on that and the governor's office and myself and I don't think anyone is wanting to go that direction."
